Ocner/TNS) MIAMI - The Houston Rockets were already at a disadvantage Monday night, playing on the second half of a road-road back-to-back against a Miami Heat team playing after a rest day and at home for the third straight game. The back-to-back meant the Rockets would be without backup center Steven Adams in addition to not having backup-backup big man Clint Capela (ankle) and Marcus Smart (suspension). Things got even more dire when Houston ruled out Amen Thompson shortly before the game with left knee soreness. Thompson's injury shouldn't be a major issue, per coach Ime Udoka, who said it's a flare up of tendinitis Thompson has managed for years. If it wasn't a back-to-back, Udoka said he was "sure" Thompson would have been able to play. Udoka declined to use the rest and injuries as an explanation, pointing to Houston's ability to weather similar issues in the early season, but the Rockets started Monday sluggish. They scored just 15 first-quarter points in a 128-110 loss to Miami at Kaseya Center. item.title: Hiding remotes and unplugging TVs: How Celebrity Race Across the World cut Jeff Stelling off from football
item.description: Jeff Stelling has revealed that producers would unplug televisions and hide remotes during filming of Celebrity Race Across the World , which left the veteran sports broadcaster completely cut off from football and his beloved Hartlepool United . Stelling is taking part in the latest series of the hit adventure travel show, teaming with his son Matt in a 4,660-mile race from the Malaysian city of Kuching to the finish line in Melbourne , Australia on a budget of £26 a day. The former Soccer Saturday presenter, who ended over 30 years of service with Sky Sports in May 2023 , is a passionate lifelong Hartlepool fan and serves as honorary president of the National League club. But as he traversed the depths of South East Asia with no phone and limited technology, he was left completely in the dark about the club’s performance at the tail-end of the 2025/26 season. “We couldn’t get any football scores at all because we’ve got no way [of finding them out],” Stelling told The Independent . “If you’re within your checkpoints, if there’s a TV in your room, they [the producers] make sure it’s either disconnected or else they don’t give you a remote, so they make sure that that’s taken away. You’ve got no contact.” The fourth series of the show, which aired its first episode on Wednesday, was filmed from February to April earlier this year. During that time, Hartlepool experienced a mixed bag of results - going on their joint-best win streak of the season with three consecutive victories, only for that run to be ended by their heaviest defeat of the season: a 7-0 hammering at Wealdstone at the end of March. Jeff Stelling (left) is a passionate lifelong Hartlepool fan (Getty) Stelling says he was out of the loop for all of this, however, which allowed him to let his dreams run wild as the National League season approached its climax. “For me, it meant I could fantasise that we were winning every game,” he added. “And then when we finished, I found out the truth that we hadn’t been winning every game.” Hartlepool ended last season in ninth, 12 points adrift of the National League play-off places. item.description: There is a changing of the guard in football punditry and the 17th floor of talkSPORT Towers provides a snapshot of its evolution. Listeners, pick your poison. In the morning, you can tune into the veteran of sports broadcasting. Jeff Stelling , once the voice of our Saturday afternoons, hosts your breakfast show alongside Ally McCoist from Mondays through to Wednesdays. It’s classic stuff. While most of his Soccer Saturday colleagues have since been consigned to the scrapheap, Stelling still very much has his foothold in the industry and as such brings us a taste of the ‘good old days’. However, his old-school bread-and-butter style admittedly feels like it’s on its way out, for better or worse. Because in the dark of the night, during the prime-time slot, things go a bit blinky-eyed manic. The seat occupied by Stelling earlier that day is now filled by a man in a mask, shouting into a microphone. Jason Cundy and Jamie O’Hara are changing the pundit’s playbook with The Sports Bar ; it’s chaotic, it’s crude and it does millions. Never one to be behind the times, Stelling recognises the market for football media based largely on mockery nowadays. But don’t expect him to follow suit. Jeff Stelling is an old-school football broadcaster in a changing age (PA Wire) “I think there’s a place for it... not on one of my shows!” Stelling tells The Independent , who will not be showing up to work with a Derek McInnes mask any time soon. “But Cundy and O’Hara, I think at that time of night... it’s irreverent to say the least. Obviously they take the mickey out of each other mercifully, Cundy with his Ange mask and so on. And they take the mickey out of callers as well. I think it works perfectly well at that stage. But you can’t have that all the way through.” Pundits increasingly find themselves leaning into their club loyalties for the sake of entertainment, when purists would argue that the position should be neutral. Stelling, admittedly, was never completely down the middle; he was and still is known for his die-hard fandom of Hartlepool United , where he serves as honorary president. It’s fuelled his love of non-league, which is why he found himself at Woking FC on this grey October afternoon, fronting Enterprise’s Local Legends campaign which strives to celebrate the volunteers that keep clubs like his alive. item.title: Will Sunderland Ever Have Another 50-Goal Striker?
item.description: 29 Apr 2000: Niall Quinn of Sunderland celebrates scoring the equalizer during the FA Carling Premiership match between Aston Villa and Sunderland at Villa Park, Birmingham. Mandatory Credit: Laurence Griffiths/ALLSPORT | Getty Images The increased turnover of players in the modern game was highlighted recently by Luke O’Nien breaking Lee Cattermole’s record for the highest number of different Sunderland teammates. In his eight years at the club, Luke has shared the pitch with 149 other players. By contrast, The Lads’ record appearance-maker, Jim Montgomery, played with fewer than a hundred colleagues in his 15-year Wearside career between 1961 and 1976. This trend has naturally meant that players are spending less time at one club and, consequently, individual appearance and goalscoring records are suffering accordingly. Only three players (Lee Cattermole, John O’Shea and Luke O’Nien) have reached the 250 first-team game mark this century, whereas seven clocked 250 in the 1990s. Aside from the latter years of the outstanding Kevin Phillips’ career, no player has threatened the 50-goal mark since Niall Quinn reached his half-century against his old club Arsenal in January 2000. Considering that the big Irishman was the 35th player to score 50 first-team goals for Sunderland, and at least one player had reached the landmark every decade since the club entered the league in 1890, there has to be doubt that anyone will reach that figure again. The reasons why no player has scored 50 goals for Sunderland in the last 26, going on 27, years are up for debate, but the club’s current operating model will probably ensure that any future prolificacy in front of goal will lead to an early and profitable sale, especially if we stay in the top tier. Since Quinny’s milestone, the one and only Kevin Phillips, who reached his first 50 goals for Sunderland in 1999, netted another 51 times and remains the club’s highest scorer in the 21st century, despite leaving the club 23 years ago. However, only one other player, Charlie Wyke, has exceeded 40 goals, let alone 50, with the top scorers list since 2000 making rather modest reading: Kevin Phillips – 51 (nos. 79-130) Charlie Wyke – 42 Ross Stewart – 40 Marcus Stewart – 39 Jermaine Defoe – 37 Darren Bent – 36 Kenwyne Jones – 28 Jack Clarke – 28 In my humble opinion, the club’s model accounted for the (arguably) premature departures of Clarke and Ross Stewart, and Darren Bent would have reached 50 if he had chosen to stay. Marcus Stewart would probably have bagged a few in the ill-fated 2005/06 season – he couldn’t have done any worse than his replacements. item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 8: Sunderland's Enzo Le Fee celebrates scoring the opening goal with his team mates during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Chelsea FC at Stadium of Light on November 8, 2026 in Sunderland, United Kingdom. (Photo by Lee Parker - CameraSport via Getty Images) | CameraSport via Getty Images I’ve had few moments of relief like that when the full-time whistle blew at the Stadium of Light last weekend. Of course, the wins against the Mags have brought elation, last season’s draw against the eventual champions gave me immense pride, and plenty of results last season brought great happiness. As my nail-biting was allowed to stop and I was able to digest the game, it became clearer why. No Sunderland fan is unfamiliar with a relegation battle, or even a drastic turn in fortune between seasons. The contrast between the success and overwhelming highs Régis Le Bris has brought and this season’s performances has left me equal parts frustrated and upset. I had almost reached the point of apathy before the Chelsea result, not because I don’t care, but because I was slowly coming to the conclusion that perhaps Le Bris had run his race on Wearside. That’s not exactly something I was ready to process yet, having done my best to avoid the uncomfortable conversations going on around me. As the team sheets rolled out and the group chats lit up, there appeared to be some common questions: “What has Ahoka got to do to start?” “Hume at right wing again?” “Why can’t he get out of his own way?” Well, what a difference a couple of hours can make. As it turns out, Régis knows what he is doing; I’m not ashamed to say I was left with egg on my face. Questions still remain, but, as a victory can often do, they are now of a different nature, or at the very least, with a different framing. “How much has this season been down to Xhaka?” “Hume on the wing, maybe not what we want, but is he what the side needs now?” “That felt like last season. What changed? And what was he trying to do before today?” Let me stress, I don’t know better than Le Bris. Le Fée (#28) was notably more conservatively positioned than in previous outings, firming up what was almost a 4-5-1 when out of possession. item.title: OTD (17/11/1991): Tensions are high in the Wear-Tyne derby
item.description: On this day, 17th November 1991, Sunderland hosted the 125th game against Newcastle, a fixture dating back to November 1888. Ossie Ardiles brought his side to Roker Park for this Second Division clash off the back of a slight improvement in form. They had been sitting bottom of the league after eleven games and only one win, but had climbed to 21st due to a haul of five points in five games. Denis Smith’s side sat mid-table with 22 points, albeit not safe by any means. As was becoming standard practice, following requests from police and local authorities, the kick-off was moved to Sunday at 12:00 due to potential crowd trouble. Tensions were high, in part down to the 1990 play-off victory at Sid James’ Park, when pitch invasions and disturbances marred our 2-0 win. Sunderland won the play-off semi-final, got promoted despite losing to Swindon in the final, then got relegated the following season, landing us back here in Division Two. Sunderland: Tony Norman (GK), John Kay, Gary Bennett, Anton Rogan, Ian Sampson, Gordon Armstrong, Paul Bracewell, Colin Pascoe, Peter Davenport, John Byrne, David Rush. Sunderland started the match well, having the better of the opening exchanges, and Davenport’s goal on 21 minutes was well deserved. A Rogan cross from the left byline was flicked on and Davenport hit a left-foot shot that looked as if it might be cleared but ended up being skewed into the net by Matty Appleby. Despite having another couple of great chances, most notably a volley from Armstrong, who, from 25 yards out, hit a dipping shot that had Tommy Wright scrambling, Sunderland couldn’t find a second. Armstrong was involved in a lot that afternoon, and another right-footed shot was well tipped over by Wright. Unfortunately, Armstrong’s final involvement of note was immediately before the equaliser. On 59 minutes, instead of clearing a ball that fell to him in midfield, his tricky footwork was read, he was tackled and the ball fell to Liam O’Brien, who chipped Tony Norman from 22 yards. Despite being the better side, with better chances and more of the ball, we had to be satisfied with a point. The largest crowd of the season to date, 29,224, included 4,000 Newcastle supporters. Housed right behind the goal in the Roker End, they saw both goals in front of them. A few pockets of Geordies had bought tickets in the Clock Stand and some skirmishes had broken out. The police got involved and removed any away fans they could find. Some went to the Roker End and some were ejected. The previously mentioned play-off in 1990 had been stopped for 21 minutes while the pitch was cleared following an invasion. Nothing of that magnitude happened, but in those days, trouble never felt far away. The 12:00 kick-off, no 24-hour licensing laws, and a huge police presence may have explained that. item.description: Nov 16, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers (4) fumbles the ball as Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Tarheeb Still (4) recovers the ball at M&T Bank Stadium. BALTIMORE — The wait is finally over. The Los Angeles Chargers are in the win column. After starting the season 0-8, Los Angeles captured its first victory over the Baltimore Ravens, 23-20, on Monday Night Football at M&T Bank Stadium. W https://t.co/MRX8yJN25u — Los Angeles Chargers (@chargers) November 17, 2026 Entering the night as the NFL's lone winless team, head coach Jim Harbaugh needed someone to step up and snap an 11-game losing streak dating back to last season (including playoffs) — a stretch that tied a franchise record for consecutive losses. Cornerback Tarheeb Still proved to be that player. With Los Angeles clinging to a three-point lead just before the two-minute warning, Baltimore quarterback Jacoby Brissett — making his first start as a Raven after being traded from the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 6 — hit star wide receiver Zay Flowers on the outside. Flowers beat Still for a first down past midfield, moving Baltimore closer to tying field-goal range. Staying with the play, Still wrapped up Flowers with the help of safety Genesis Smith and ripped the ball out of the former first-round pick's hands. item.title: 3 Ravens to blame for becoming first Chargers victim in 2026 NFL season
item.description: Jesse Minter and Derrick Henry . 3 Ravens to blame for becoming first Chargers victim in 2026 NFL season appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Baltimore Ravens are 4-6 on the 2026 NFL season after dropping Monday Night Football’s November 16 home game at M&T Bank Stadium to the Los Angeles Chargers, who scored their first win of the season on a night when Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton took a worrying blow to the head . The Chargers jumped out to a 10-0 lead before running back Derrick Henry tied Marshall Faulk for seventh most touchdowns in NFL history. Baltimore is now fourth place in the AFC North , headed into Week 11’s road game against Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers. The Chargers were fired up to get their first win of the season in nine tries, but that doesn’t excuse the brutal effort turned in by the Ravens on Monday Night Football. Ravens coach Jesse Minter is a neophyte among NFL head coaches, but that isn’t an excuse for the way his team played. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) There is a lot of blame to go around from Week 10’s colossal failure in front of the hometown faithful, and the buck stops with the Ravens’ head man. Raven to blame #1: Jesse Minter Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Minter had a lot of familiarity with Harbaugh’s Chargers from his days as his defensive coordinator in Los Angeles and at the University of Michigan, but it appeared to work against him in this game as Minter’s defense was shredded by the revitalized Chargers in the first half. Justin Herbert started off the scoring with a 22-yard touchdown run while Omarion Hampton looked like the future All-Pro everyone thought he would be after his rookie season again. The Hampton and Herbert duo was too much for the Ravens as they scrambled to keep pace. item.title: Canucks Pull Off Historic Win In Utah, Defeat The Mammoth 3-2
item.description: The Vancouver Canucks picked up their second straight win on Monday as they defeated the Utah Mammoth 3-2. Jake DeBrusk and Brock Boeser each scored on the power play while Filip Chytil picked up his third goal over the last two games. As for in net, Nikita Tolopilo was a star in his first game of the campaign as he stopped 34 of the 36 shots he faced. Monday's win was a historic one as it was the first time the Canucks have defeated the Mammoth . Vancouver entered Monday with a 0-5-1 all-time record against Utah, which included being outscored 25 to 11. Despite being the tired team, the Canucks found a way to take down the Mammoth and pick up their fifth victory of the season. The main reason Vancouver picked up this win was Tolopilo's play. The 26-year-old made multiple highlight-reel saves and came up big whenever the Canucks needed him. Based on Monday's performance, it will be hard to justify sending Tolopilo back to the Abbotsford Canucks right away. Chytil is also starting to kick his game into high gear. He created multiple breakaway opportunities, while his goal came from what looked like an impossible angle on a wrap-around. One part of Chytil's game that isn't being talked about is his work on the penalty kill, as he logged 2:53 of shorthanded time on Monday night. Vancouver's power play was also a bright spot as they went two for four on the night. The Canucks also managed six shots on the man advantage, with DeBrusk leading the way with three. Vancouver's penalty kill was also solid despite giving up a goal as they killed four of five opportunities while only allowing eight shots. While this was not a masterpiece from a defensive perspective, the Canucks found a way to bend but not break in Salt Lake City. Wins like the one on Monday are important for a rebuild, as the group was able to bounce back from goals allowed and never trailed in the game. The victory also secured Vancouver's first win streak of the season as they went two for two on back-to-back nights. item.description: Can teams trade players even after the IPL 2026 retention deadline and before the mini auction? Rules explained originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The days leading up to the IPL 2027 retention deadline on November 17 saw plenty of player trades and cash deals among teams. The highlight, however, was the high-profile deal between Punjab Kings (PBKS) and Mumbai Indians (MI). Hardik Pandya moved to PBKS and as part of the swap deal, MI received two star India fast bowler Arshdeep Singh. We take a look at the rules governing trade deals and the deadlines for the trade window. What is an IPL trade window? An IPL trade window is the period in which franchises can move contracted players between themselves without going through an auction. Unlike a bidding war, a trade is a negotiated deal, so a team can target one specific player rather than hope the room lets him come cheap. There are two types. A player-for-player swap sends cricketers in both directions, with the contract amounts adjusted if the sides agree, while an all-cash trade sees one franchise sign a contracted player and pay the other a transfer fee without sending anyone back. The process runs through the BCCI rather than between the clubs alone. The interested franchise submits an Expression of Interest, the player's current team has 48 hours to respond, and if it agrees the player has to sign a consent form before terms are settled and the board approves the move. That consent is the part franchises cannot work around. A contracted player cannot be forced into a trade, and if a fee is reduced, he has to agree in writing, with the selling franchise covering the difference for that season. Can teams trade players after the IPL 2027 retention deadline? Yes. The retention deadline and the trade window are separate dates, and submitting a retained and released list on November 17 does not stop a franchise from trading afterwards. The first window of this cycle runs from seven days after the end of the previous season until seven days before the auction, which means it closes on December 9, 2026, more than three weeks after the retention lists are filed. Everything completed so far, including the Rishabh Pant and Kuldeep Yadav swap and the four-player deal between Chennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad, has happened inside it. The second window opens the day after the auction, on December 17, and stays open until 30 days before the new season begins. It exists so franchises can fix whatever the auction left unbalanced, though it comes with the tightest restriction in the system, as a player bought at that auction cannot be traded for the season immediately after it. A few other rules apply throughout. Overseas players need a No Objection Certificate from their national board, injured players can be traded but the buying franchise may insist on a medical, and the BCCI can reject a deal outright. As it stands, the prevailing discussion is that the Pens are open for business. They’re willing to listen on just about anyone. And, as long as the price is right, they are willing to make moves happen. That’s why the Penguins forward could become an intriguing alternative for teams looking to add depth down the middle. Novak has seven goals and 14 points in 19 games, and he can play both center and wing. He’s also been used on the power play and penalty kill. His versatility makes him potentially attractive to teams looking for additional forward depth. That’s why clubs looking for flexibility might just have the sort of player that can fill multiple middle-six roles without necessarily costing an arm and a leg. Sure, Novak might not be the sexiest name out there. But contenders looking to shore up their forward depth could do a heck of a lot worse than Tommy Novak. Novak Has an Attractive Contract for Potential Suitors The most attractive aspect about Tommy Novak is his contract. Yes, he’s got plenty of skills to help any team round out their lineup.
